value.rationale: The exact inverse-leading channel switch is a substantive implementation design choice. A well-conditioned indefinite system can induce premature mixed-channel failure while a third independent extended Krylov vector exists, so stopping at a zero coefficient can be misleading. The sharp normalized scalar threshold identifies all possible local step-three comparisons and a linear arbitrarily-severe near-breakdown regime, furnishing concrete safeguards and test cases. Applicability is explicitly limited to this step and metric; global accuracy and floating-point failure rates are not asserted.
